before: Wirtz et al (2018) divide service tasks into two classes, namely, routine services and emotional and social judgment services. Their system will allow automated checks and still keep employees on the job for cases that need them. These predictions don't establish local customer acceptance. Company publications are about initiatives, not autonomous satisfaction tests. To scale up, Carrefour UAE should measure the performance of the tasks and the effort required by customers. Carrefour's examples include conversational advice, which is also being automated. The recommendation effects were found to differ depending on the frequency of visiting the bakery in a bakery study (Song et al., 2024). It has a remotely controlled robot, which restricts drawing conclusions about autonomous performance.

before: Personalization introduces a paradox – between the benefit of suggestions and the volume of data collected. Purchase history as an aid to recommendations (Brazil's Nutri Choice, Carrefour 2021). These records could also show the UAE assistant assistant's delicate dietary preferences if they are proposing to move to the UAE. Guest mode should be functioning properly at levels 1 and 4 without saving a purchase profile. Independent consent for saved preferences and marketing would allow consumers to opt-in for convenience without compromising on irrelevant information. Short retention and limited access would limit exposure, but would also limit the amount of historical data which would undermine the personalisation.

before: Commercial interests may also impact recommendations. However, Huang and Rust (2021) caution that optimization might lead to biased answers when no explicit instructions are given to discriminate. If Carrefour chooses the profit margin route then it may prove harder to locate alternatives suitable and cheap products. Retailer should label sponsored offers and enable unit price sorting. The shoppers have the last say. Advertising should not rely on consumers being confused by advertising for the same content as non-advertising sources.
after: Commercial interests may also impact recommendations. Huang and Rust (2021) caution that optimization might lead to biased answers even without instructions to discriminate. If Carrefour prioritises profit margins, it may be harder to find suitable, cheaper products. The retailer should label sponsored offers and enable unit price sorting. The shoppers have the last say. Advertising should not rely on consumers mistaking sponsored advice for neutral information.

before: Physical robotics doesn't impact just app users. Some of the issues highlighted by Wirtz et al. (2018) involve privacy and security concerns from robots' sensing abilities. At stage 3, identifiable shoppers should be minimised and incidental images used and kept to a minimum. The robot shall give way to humans and must be easily stopped. Staffed assistance and Readable Instructions provide protection for customers who may lack digital confidence, language barriers or disabilities at F3. Equal access is expensive, self-service is free and it would be unfair to put the burden of such a business on those who can't afford it.
after: Wirtz et al. (2018) highlight privacy and security concerns from robots' sensing abilities. At stage 3, recording identifiable shoppers and retaining incidental images should be minimised. The robot should give way to people and be easily stopped. Staffed assistance and readable instructions support customers with limited digital confidence, language barriers or disabilities at F3. Equal access costs money, but self-service savings should not depend on excluding those who cannot use it.

before: Employees can save time with the automated checks, but now get more alerts, monitoring and hard-to-handle customer cases. Carrefour needs to take its shelf staff into consideration when designing alerts, pay for them to be trained, and track workload and response time. If there is no stock then an unresolved alert should not be considered poor employee performance. Managers continue to be responsible for staffing and recovery, and this does not absolve their duty to customers from using third party software. Alerts that are wrong can lead to greater integration and maintenance costs. During this test of this risk, a limited pilot provides for service continuity. The rank and workload should be audited weekly for managers.
after: Employees can save time with the automated checks, but now get more alerts, monitoring and hard-to-handle customer cases. Carrefour needs to involve shelf staff when designing alerts, fund their training, and track workload and response time. Without stock, an unresolved alert should not be considered poor employee performance. Managers continue to be responsible for staffing and recovery, and third-party software does not remove their duty to customers. Incorrect alerts can increase integration and maintenance costs. A limited pilot protects service continuity while testing this risk. Rankings and workload should be audited weekly by managers.
